answer: Go to Calendar, click any time slot, pick the client, service, and staff member, then confirm the date and time. New appointments default to "Booked" status until payment or confirmation changes it.
Click the appointment on the calendar and select Edit to change the date/time. You can also drag-and-drop the appointment card directly to a new slot in Day or Week view.
Click the appointment in the calendar and select Cancel or Delete, then confirm. Cancelled bookings are logged but removed from the active calendar view.

Appointment status can be Booked (created, nothing paid yet), Partial (deposit or part-payment collected), Paid (fully paid), Cancelled, No Show (client didn't arrive), or Deleted. There's no separate "Confirmed" or "In Progress" state — an unpaid Booked appointment automatically flips to No Show once its end time passes.
When creating or editing an appointment, use the Notes field to add special instructions. These are visible to the assigned staff member before and during the appointment.
Go to Calendar and switch to Day View. Use the date navigation arrows or click the date to jump to a specific day. All appointments for that day appear in the time grid.

Yes — when creating an appointment, you can add multiple services to the same booking, each with its own staff member. Review the time slot before confirming since each service's own duration affects how the booking fits on the calendar.
Yes — when creating or editing an appointment, select a colour from the colour picker. This helps you visually identify different service types or staff on the calendar.

Click the appointment on the calendar and change its status to No Show. Unpaid "Booked" appointments left open past their end time are also flipped to No Show automatically, so you won't always need to do this by hand.
In Calendar, click the Week View toggle in the top bar. You'll see all staff columns side by side across the week, making it easy to spot availability gaps.
You can leave the client field empty when creating an appointment. The booking will still appear on the calendar and can be linked to a client later when they arrive.

There's no separate "Confirmed" status in the system — appointments start as Booked and move to Partial or Paid once payment is taken, or to Cancelled/No Show if the visit doesn't happen. Acknowledge the booking with the client over a call or WhatsApp rather than through a status change.
In the Calendar top bar, use the staff filter to select a specific team member. The calendar will show only their appointments for the selected view (day/week/month).
Open the appointment's bill and use the Print/Receipt option. A formatted receipt is generated that you can print or share with the client once the sale is paid.
Open the sale, click Checkout, choose the payment method (Cash, Card, UPI, eWallet, Gift Card, or Split), add a reference if needed, and confirm. The sale status changes to Completed once fully paid.

Supported payment methods are Cash, Card, UPI, eWallet, Gift Card, Package/Membership balance, and Split (multiple methods combined in one transaction). You can also record a payment reference number for traceability.
When editing a sale, enter the amount in the Discount field. You can apply it at the overall sale level or per individual line item (service or product).
In the sale or checkout screen, enter the amount in the Tip Amount field before completing payment. Tips are tracked separately and included in staff commission reports.
Open the completed sale and change its status to Refunded. Note the original payment method — the actual refund must be issued through that same channel (cash/card/UPI) manually.
Go to Sales > Daily Sales. Use the date arrows to navigate or click Today. You'll see all transactions, payment method breakdown, and a cash movement summary.
Go to Sales > Quick Sale. Add the services or products, optionally link a client, and proceed to checkout. Quick sales are tracked in daily sales reports alongside appointment-based sales.

Yes — sales support a tax amount, calculated using the tax rates configured in Settings > Tax Mapping. The tax is added to the total and shown separately on the receipt, and appears in the GST Report under Reports > Sales.
At checkout, select Split as the payment method. You can then enter how much is paid via each method (e.g. ₹500 cash + ₹300 UPI). Every method used is recorded in the transaction.
Go to Sales > Sales List. You can filter by date range, client, or status (Draft, Completed, Cancelled, Refunded). Click any sale to view its full itemised details.
A Draft sale has been created but checkout has not been completed — the client has not been charged. Open the sale and click Checkout to finalise the payment.
On the Daily Sales or Sales List page, click Export. You can download as PDF, Excel, or text. Choose your date range before exporting for a scoped report.
Go to Clients > Add. Enter the client's full name (required), phone, and email. They'll appear in the list and can be selected when booking appointments.
In Clients, select the client(s), then Options > Block Customers and provide a reason. Blocked clients can't be added to bookings. You can unblock anytime from the same menu.
Go to Clients > Options > Merge Clients. Select the primary record to keep and the duplicate. The primary absorbs the duplicate's history. This cannot be undone.
Go to Clients > Options > Import Clients. Upload a CSV or Excel file with columns for name, phone, and email. The system validates and imports all valid records.
Click any client in the Clients list to open their profile. You'll see their full booking history, past sales, tags, notes, and WhatsApp communication log linked to their account.
In the Clients list, go to Options > Export. Your client data (name, phone, email, sales, and creation date) will be downloaded as a CSV or Excel file.
Select the client(s) in the Clients list, then Options > Add Tags. You can create custom tags like "VIP", "Regular", or "Bride" to segment clients for marketing campaigns.
Click the client in the Clients list to open their profile, then click Edit. Update their name, phone, email, or any other detail, and save the changes.
Select the client in the Clients list, go to Options > Delete. Confirm the deletion. Note: this permanently removes the client's record and cannot be undone.
Use the search bar at the top of the Clients page. You can search by name, phone number, or email. Results filter in real time as you type.

Go to Team > Staff Members > Add. Fill in first name, email (required), plus phone and job title. After the staff member is created, open their profile to configure wages, commission, schedule, and blocked times.

Go to Team > Scheduled Shifts to set up each staff member's working hours for the week. There's no separate "repeating shifts" screen — you set the schedule once per staff member and it stays in effect going forward until changed.

Commission is configured per staff member by category — Services, Products, Memberships, Gift Cards, and Cancellation — under Team > Commissions, as a percentage or fixed rate. If your salon has set up Commission Rules (a newer rules engine with milestone/threshold-based payouts), an active rule for that staff member takes priority over their basic per-category rate for the calculation.

Go to Team > Payroll. Create a payroll entry for the staff member and period, review attendance and commission summaries, then mark it Paid once wages are processed. Salary advances can also be recorded from the same section.

In the staff profile, go to Leaves and add a time-off entry with the date range and leave type. This is separate from Blocked Times, which blocks only part of a single day rather than a full leave period.

Which services a staff member performs is managed from the Catalog/Services side rather than at staff creation — check the service's own settings for who can perform it. On the calendar, a staff member also needs a matching schedule and branch, and no blocked time, to be bookable for a given slot.
Go to Team > Attendance. You'll see daily check-in/check-out records, status, and hours worked per staff member, with monthly and date-range views plus export.
In the staff profile, go to the Wages section. You can set a compensation type of hourly, salary, or commission-only. This feeds into Payroll when calculating what's owed for a period.
Staff can be linked to a business location as part of their profile. They'll only appear on the calendar for bookings at their assigned location.

Go to Team > Scheduled Shifts to set each staff member's working days and hours. The schedule you set stays in effect going forward — there isn't a separate weekly "repeating shifts" screen, it's the same schedule view.
Go to Marketing > Settings. Enter your Phone Number ID, WABA ID, App ID, and Access Token from Meta Business Manager. Once verified, you can create templates and run campaigns.

Go to Marketing > Templates > Create. Add the name, category (Marketing/Utility/Authentication), language, and body text. Optionally add a header and buttons. Submit for Meta approval — usually takes minutes to 24 hours.
Check the rejection reason in the template details. Common causes: promotional language in a Utility template, policy violation, or unclear variable usage. Revise the content and resubmit.

Go to Marketing > Campaigns > Create. Select an approved template, add your contact list with each contact's phone number and any template variables, set a batch size, and launch. Monitor delivery in real time on the campaign page.

Open the campaign from Marketing > Campaigns. You'll see Sent, Delivered, Read, Failed, and Blocked counts. The WA Marketing Campaign report under Reports > Marketing gives read rates and engagement across all campaigns.
Open the campaign from Marketing > Campaigns and click the Pause button. The campaign status will change to Paused and no further messages will be sent until you resume it.
Your daily limit is set by Meta based on your WhatsApp Business account tier. You can view your current daily limit in Marketing > Settings under your WhatsApp Config details.

Quality rating (Green/Yellow/Red) reflects how recipients respond to your messages. Green = good standing. Yellow = some blocks/complaints. Red = high complaints — may restrict sending. Avoid sending too frequently to unresponsive contacts.

When creating a template, select Image, Video, or Document as the header type and upload the file. The media is uploaded to Meta and a handle is generated. This is required before you can submit the template for approval.

Open a specific campaign's detail page to see each message's delivery event: Sent, Delivered, Read, Failed, or Blocked, along with the timestamp for each status update. A client's full WhatsApp message history (automation plus campaigns) is also visible on their profile's Communication tab.
Go to Catalog > Services > Add. Enter the name, category, price, and duration. The service will appear when booking appointments and in Quick Sale.

Go to Catalog > Products > Add. Fill in the product name, price, and stock quantity — you can also set an expiry date if the product has one. Products can be sold at checkout alongside services and are tracked in inventory reports.

Go to Catalog > Memberships > Add. Define the name, price, which services or categories it applies to, number of sessions (or unlimited), and an optional expiry date. Clients are enrolled by selling the membership at checkout, which creates their own membership instance with its own remaining sessions or wallet balance.

Gift Card is available as a payment method at checkout for accepting a gift card as payment. There isn't a separate gift card issuing/balance-management screen in the catalog — check with your salon's process for how gift cards are issued and tracked.
Go to Catalog > Categories > Add. Create categories like Hair, Skin, or Nails. When adding a service, assign it to the relevant category so it's easy to find during booking.
Go to Catalog > Services, find the service, and click Edit. Update the price field and save. The new price will apply to all future bookings and sales.
Go to Catalog > Services, find the service, and click Edit. Update the Duration (in minutes) and save. The new duration will be used when calculating appointment end times.
Go to Catalog > Services, find the service, and click Delete. Confirm the action. Deleting a service won't affect historical sales or past appointments that included it.

Go to Settings > Business. Update your salon name, contact info, and other business details. For your public-facing profile (used for the marketplace/online booking page), edit it separately from Dashboard > Online Booking > Marketplace Profile.
On the login page, click "Forgot Password" and enter your registered email. You'll receive a reset link. Check your spam folder if you don't see it within a few minutes.

Go to Team > Staff Members > Add, fill in their details, and save. They'll receive an invitation email to join your account with their assigned role and permissions, which they accept to set up their own login.

Go to Settings > Integrations, or Dashboard > Online Booking for specific connections like Reserve with Google and Facebook & Instagram. Available connections let clients discover and book your salon from outside the app.

The system supports multiple business locations, and staff can be linked to a specific branch so they only appear on that branch's calendar. Contact SalonOx support to have an additional branch set up on your account.
Go to Settings > Account & Security. Update your email or phone number. You may need to verify the new contact via OTP before the change is applied.
On the Login page, click "Continue with Google" or the equivalent social login option. On first use, you'll be redirected to authorise access, and your account will be linked for future logins.
Click the invitation link sent by your manager. It will open the Join Business page where you create your staff profile. Once approved, you'll have access based on your assigned role.

Go to Reports and open the Sales category. Sales Summary shows every bill for a period with totals, payments and balances, while Daily Sheet shows a single day's transactions. The main Dashboard also has a revenue summary card for a quick overview.
Go to Reports > Sales > Service Sale. It shows every service sold, with count, revenue, and average ticket per service, so you can identify your highest-performing offerings.

Go to Reports > Appointments. Detailed Appointment Reports shows every appointment for a period with status, staff, service and payment detail, and Upcoming Appointments Report lists what's still booked ahead.

Go to Reports > Staff > Staff Performance for one row per staff member with invoices, revenue, commission, and amounts collected/due. Staff Sales breaks revenue down by service and product per staff member.
There isn't a dedicated gift card report — gift card payments show up in the Sales Summary and Daily Sheet reports (Reports > Sales) under the Gift Card payment method breakdown.

Go to Reports > Package and Membership. Membership Sale shows memberships purchased by clients and their current status, and Membership History shows redemption-by-redemption usage for every client membership.
On any report page, use the Export option to download as PDF or Excel. Set your date range before exporting to get a scoped report for the period you need.

Go to Reports > Payments > Payment Collection Report for outstanding balances per bill, or check the Sales Summary and Daily Sheet reports under Reports > Sales for a payment-method breakdown of revenue collected.

Go to Enquiries > Add. Enter the person's name and phone, and optionally the service and staff they're interested in. Each enquiry gets a status of New, Follow-up, Converted, or Closed so you can track it through to booking.

Open the enquiry from the Enquiries list and update its status — move it to Follow-up while you're in touch, Converted once they book or become a client, or Closed if it doesn't go anywhere. You can also set a follow-up date and add notes.
On the Enquiries page, use the search box and status filter to narrow the list, and the date range filter to look at enquiries from a specific period.

Turn on Reward Points from Settings > Reward Points and set how much a client must spend to earn points, and how many points equal how much rupee value off a future bill. Once active, points are earned automatically on sales and can be redeemed at checkout; each client's point history is on their profile and in Reports > Sales > Reward.

Check that Reward Points is turned on in Settings > Reward Points, and that the sale amount met the configured spend threshold to earn points. Check the client's point ledger on their profile to see every earn/redeem/adjustment entry with the reason.

Open the client's profile and use the eWallet section to top up their balance — enter the amount and the payment method used to collect it. The balance can then be used as "eWallet" at checkout on future visits, and every top-up/redemption is logged in the wallet ledger.

Open the client's profile, go to eWallet, and use Adjust to credit or debit the balance manually — a reason is required so there's an audit trail for the correction. Check the wallet ledger and the balance breakdown (which separates referral rewards, reward-point credits, and other credits) to see exactly where the balance came from before adjusting.

Turn on Refer & Earn from Settings > Refer & Earn and set the reward amount for both the referrer and the new client, plus the minimum first-bill amount required to unlock it. Each client gets a referral code, and both rewards are credited to eWallet balance once the referred client's first qualifying bill is paid.

Check that Refer & Earn is active in Settings > Refer & Earn, and that the new client's first bill meets the configured minimum amount — the reward is only credited after that bill is paid. Check the client's referral ledger on their profile for the earn/redeem history.

Go to Settings > Coupons to create a coupon with a code, discount type (percentage or flat), value, minimum order amount, and expiry date. At checkout or during validation, enter the code to apply the discount to the bill.

In Settings > Coupons, use the bulk creation option to generate a batch of coupons at once — set a code prefix, how many to create, and the shared discount rules. You can delete an entire batch later using its batch label.

Check that the coupon hasn't expired, is marked active, and that the order total meets its minimum order amount and hasn't hit its max uses. Coupon codes are validated at the point of entry, so a typo in the code is the most common reason it's rejected.

Go to Marketing > Coupon Designer to create shareable coupon artwork — pick a template, add text, backgrounds, shapes and QR/barcodes, and it pulls your salon's logo and social handles automatically. You can duplicate a design or export it as an image once finished.

A Membership plan is usually a wallet-style or percentage-discount benefit tied to a category of services, while a Package is a fixed bundle of specific services sold with a set number of sessions each. When a client buys either, it creates their own instance with its own remaining sessions or balance, separate from the salon's reusable plan/template.

Set up a reusable Package Template first (name, services with session counts, price, and expiry) from Settings > Packages, then sell it to a client via Quick Sale or Calendar's "+ Package" option. Each sold package tracks remaining sessions per service and can optionally schedule the first appointment right away.

When billing an appointment that's covered by a client's package, the matching service session is deducted automatically. You can also mark a session as completed directly from the client's package record, which records which staff member performed it.

Go to Cash Management and click Open Counter to start the day with an opening cash balance. Log any cash expenses during the day, then click Close Counter at end of day, enter the actual in-store cash counted, and the system reconciles it against expected cash revenue.
With a cash counter open, go to Cash Management > Expenses and add an entry with the expense type, amount, and date. This is deducted from the day's cash revenue when you close the counter.

When you close the counter, enter the actual cash counted in the drawer — the system compares it to the expected closing balance (opening balance plus cash revenue minus cash expenses) and shows the reconciliation difference. Review the day's cash sales and logged expenses if there's a mismatch.

After a visit, clients can be sent a WhatsApp feedback link where they rate their experience and leave comments — this also collects per-service and per-staff ratings. Reviews and average ratings are visible under Reviews (owner/admin access).
Go to Reviews to see all client feedback with ratings and comments. From there you can view stats like average rating and total reviews for your salon.

On a client's profile, use the Notes section to add an internal note — useful for allergies, preferences, or anything staff should know before the next visit. Notes show who wrote them and can be edited or deleted later.
On a client's profile, open the Communication tab to see every WhatsApp message sent to them — both automated (like reminders) and from campaigns — along with delivery and read status.

On the Calendar, use Block Time to mark part of a staff member's day as unavailable (e.g. a lunch break), with a reason. This is different from a full day off — for that, use Leaves in the staff profile instead.
Go to Dashboard > Online Booking > Link Builder to generate a booking link you can share with clients — you can generate a general link, or one pre-filtered to a specific service or staff member.

Go to Dashboard > Online Booking > Marketplace Profile to fill in your business essentials, description, location, working hours, photos, and amenities, then click Publish to make your salon discoverable for online booking. Reserve with Google and Facebook & Instagram under the same section connect that profile to those platforms.

Go to Settings > Notifications to manage what you get notified about. In-app notifications (like new bookings) also show with an unread count in the Notifications page, and push notifications work if you've registered a device.
Go to Settings > Roles & Permissions to control what each role (owner, manager, staff) can view and do — Calendar, Sales, Clients, Catalog, Reports, and more each have their own permission toggles.

Commission Rules let you set up more advanced commission logic than the basic per-category rate — percentage, fixed, or milestone-based payouts, scoped to the whole salon, a specific staff member, or a role, with an optional revenue/count threshold. When an active rule applies to a staff member, it's used instead of their basic commission setting.

The calendar highlights conflicts. Either choose a different staff member or adjust their scheduled shift first. Staff can only be booked during their defined working hours, and not during any Blocked Time or Leave.
Go to Clients, find the client, and choose Options > Unblock Customers. Confirm the unblock. They can then be added to new appointments.
Error 131049 is a Meta recipient-level rate limit — the recipient's number has been messaged too frequently. Wait 24 hours and retry. This cannot be bypassed by the platform.
Open the draft sale, verify the items, and click Checkout to process payment. The status will change to Completed once payment is confirmed.

Check: (1) they have a scheduled shift covering that day/time, (2) they don't have a Blocked Time or Leave over that slot, and (3) their assigned branch matches the booking location. All three must line up for them to be bookable.
Use Clients > Options > Merge Clients. Select the primary (correct) record — it absorbs the duplicate's data. This cannot be undone, so verify before confirming.

Check: (1) invalid phone numbers in your contact list, (2) numbers not registered on WhatsApp, (3) Meta quality rating — if it's Red, sending is restricted. Open the campaign detail page to see the failure reason per message.
Refresh the page first. Check your internet connection. If it persists, wait a minute — there may be a brief backend outage. If the issue continues for more than 5 minutes, contact support.

Wait 30 seconds and click Resend OTP. If it still doesn't arrive, check if the phone number is correct. If using an internet-based SIM, SMS delivery may be delayed — try again or use the Google login option.
Ensure your business details are correctly set in Settings > Business. All appointment times are displayed based on the salon's configured settings, not your device timezone.

Gift Card is a payment method selected at checkout rather than a balance-tracked catalog item, so double check the amount being charged to it is correct on the bill. If it's rejecting entirely, try another payment method and check with support for how gift cards are set up on your account.

Check that the service is included in the client's membership plan (or its category, if restricted). Also verify the membership is still Active and not Expired or Exhausted — open the client's profile to see their membership status and remaining balance.

Deleting a coupon batch removes every coupon created in that batch and cannot be undone, so double-check the batch label before deleting. If a single coupon still needs to work, create it again individually rather than re-running the whole batch.

triggers: reward points not showing on client
answer: Reward Points only starts tracking once it's turned on in Settings > Reward Points — points aren't earned retroactively for sales made before it was active. If a client isn't seeing points, confirm the feature is active and their sale happened after it was turned on.

A wallet top-up requires both an amount and a payment method to be recorded, since it represents real money collected. Check the client's wallet ledger to confirm the top-up entry exists — if it's missing, the top-up wasn't completed and needs to be re-entered.

A package session is only deducted once the linked appointment is marked completed, not when it's just booked. If a package closed earlier than expected, check whether it has an early-cap setting (expire after a set number of total completed sessions) configured on its template.

Only one cash counter can be open at a time per salon, so make sure a previous session was properly closed before opening a new one. When closing, you must enter the actual in-store cash counted — the counter can't be closed without that figure.

A banner across the dashboard means SalonOx is running scheduled maintenance or has an announcement active for that time window — it's informational and doesn't block you from using the app unless stated otherwise. It will disappear automatically once the announcement's end time passes.
